title: Main spindle bearing seats, M1 as-built -- two-stage thermal shrink fit, the configuration that slipped

joint.configuration: M1 as-built (superseded by M2; retained because it is the FAILURE case)
joint.question: Same question as the M2 stack -- does either shrink-fit joint reach zero interference at any corner? -- asked of the configuration that actually slipped, so that the M2 change can be read against something.
joint.why_this_stack_exists: M1 is not a live design and nothing here is a decision input for it. It is the CONTROL. Jeff's account is that bearings and sleeves slipped and rotated under certain conditions and that this analysis validated the fix ahead of system-level testing; a fix is only validated against the thing it fixed. Modelling both configurations with the same code is also the only way to show that the archetype distinguishes them -- if M1 and M2 read the same, the model is not measuring what the failure was about.

joint.identification_note: INFERRED, and more weakly than the M2 stack's. The M1 part numbers come only from the workbook's comment column -- O13 '212966-004', O14 'wear ring: 214955-002 (M1 and M2 original is same, M2 becoming -003)', O31 '212966-004', O32 'wear ring: 214959-002'. NO DRAWING IS IN HAND for 212966-004 or 214955-002, so two of the five parts are identified by a spreadsheet comment and nothing else. The upper seat's parts and both bearings ARE the same part numbers the M2 stack traces to drawings. SOP trap 12 applies to that comment column and was checked: these comments are in column O against the row they describe (O13 names the hub on the hub-bore row, O14 the sleeve on the sleeve-thickness row), not a free-floating list, so reading them positionally is safe here -- unlike the 260729 workbook's comments column, which is a loose hardware list and is not row-aligned.
joint.clamped: Same construction as M2: two independent shrink-fit chains, retained by interference alone.
out_of_scope: Everything the M2 stack excludes, identically: the bearing-bore-to-spindle fit and the spindle sleeves (scope boundary, a separate team's joint), all axial dimensions and preload, the sleeve flange, hoop stress and contact pressure, surface roughness, coating thickness, and the bearings' internal geometry.

WHY M1 slipped. This stack shows that M1's loosest corners reach clearance; it does not establish that clearance was the root cause. The workbook's own Decision Matrix sheet lists FOUR candidate root causes -- axial gap causing loss of preload, radial gap under thermal expansion, inadequate hub seat stiffness, and combinations -- and only the second is a tolerance question. Reading this stack as the root-cause finding would be reading past the workbook's own author.

notes: CHECKS ARE GENERATED. Same as the M2 stack -- load with tolerance_stack.thermal.load_thermal_fit_stack(); interference is POSITIVE here and negative in the workbook.

THIS STACK DOES NOT REPRODUCE THE WORKBOOK'S ROW-18 SLIP, deliberately. The M1 sheet builds its LOWER seat's LMC sleeve OD from the MMC column (D18 = E17 + 2*E15, filled across to H18 and L18), so its LMC column carries more interference than its nominal column -- backwards for a least-material corner. A stack models the design, not the spreadsheet, so the arithmetic here is correct and the slip is pinned where it belongs, in tests/test_hub_bearing_rederivation.py::test_m1_lower_lmc_sleeve_od_is_a_workbook_slip. Consequence: for the M1 lower seat only, this stack's coherent-LMC comparison differs from the workbook's cached cell by 0.05 mm ON TOP of the stage-1 methodological difference. The correction does not rescue M1 -- its hot corners are clearances either way, by an order of magnitude more.

THE UPPER SEAT IS IDENTICAL TO M2's, element for element, and a test asserts that rows 31-44 are NUMERICALLY identical between the two sheets. Not byte-identical: the comment column differs, and the difference matters here -- O31 names 212966-004 on this sheet and 212966-005 on M2, which is exactly why this stack's hub_bore_upper is `inferred` where M2's is `traced` on the same numbers. So every upper-seat number in this file also appears in the M2 stack, and the M2 change touched the lower seat only.

CONFIDENCE IS LOWER HERE THAN IN THE M2 STACK AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE, not an omission: the two M1-specific parts have no drawing in the repo. The lower sleeve's bore and wall are `untraced` -- workbook-only, listed as gaps. The hub bores are `inferred`, on the strength of a later revision of the same drawing carrying the identical callout, which is corroboration and not a trace.

SAME OUT-OF-SCOPE SET AND SAME CAVEATS as the M2 stack: no nut or cotter pin so the SOP's quantised-constraint caveat does not apply; a dimensional interference is not a torque capacity; RSS is a relative softening indicator and temperature is a scenario, not a variate.

elements.name: hub lower bearing-seat bore, M1 hub 212966-004

source_ref.cell: C13, with the band from D13/E13 (=C13+0.015 / =C13-0.015)
source_ref.note: 212966-004 is not in the repo. INFERRED, not traced, and the inference is stated so it can be rejected: 212966-006 rev A (two revisions later, in hand) prints '⌀ 202.140 ±0.015' at sheet 3 DETAIL E zone C9, identical to the workbook's value AND band. A later revision of the same drawing carrying the same callout is real corroboration that the workbook transcribed its own revision correctly, but it is NOT evidence about 212966-004 -- the bore could have changed at -005 and changed back. Downgrade to untraced if that is not accepted; the 212966-004 drawing closes it either way and is listed as a gap.

temperature_source.note: The D7 annotation lives on THIS sheet -- the M1 as-built one -- which is consistent with 72 C being an observation from the M1 whirly test rather than a design requirement. Both sheets use the same 72 C. Listed as a gap; the hot case is the governing corner.

chains.label: LOWER bearing seat, M1 (hub bore 202.140 / sleeve 214955-002 / bearing 214589-002)

source_ref.callout: stiffness ratio 0.8 -- 'what fraction of interference is imposed on wear ring (estimate)'
source_ref.note: Same value and same 'estimate' label as the M2 sheet, even though the M1 sleeve is 0.065 mm thinner and therefore less stiff. A stiffness ratio that does not move when the member's thickness changes by 6% is a further sign it is judgement rather than calculation -- and it is the M1 configuration where the number matters least, because M1's clearances at hot are an order of magnitude larger than the sensitivity to k.
